gp180.choicePolicy: Since the source is purely acoustic, this rig simulates a clean, intimate fingerstyle sound using an acoustic-friendly signal chain and room ambience, compensating for the lack of true acoustic modeling.
gp180.bestMatchSummary: A highly clean, low-gain signal path utilizing compression and a gentle EQ boost to mimic the warmth and clarity of recorded acoustic fingerpicking in a natural, dry room setting.

blocks.purpose: Clean up any unwanted background noise or hum.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for clean recordings.

blocks.purpose: Smooth out the dynamics of fingerpicked arpeggios and add sustain, mimicking close-mic recording warmth.
blocks.gap: The ideal module would be a dedicated acoustic compressor. Comp is the best available choice for dynamic leveling.

blocks.purpose: Keep the signal path completely clean and transparent to avoid any coloration or grit.
blocks.gap: N/A. No drive is desired.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the fundamental warmth (low-mids) and clarity (highs) characteristic of acoustic recordings, while slightly reducing harshness.
blocks.gap: A dedicated acoustic EQ would be better, but Guitar EQ 1 allows for precise frequency shaping needed for this genre.

blocks.purpose: Select a clean, vintage-voiced amplifier model that is known for its natural and non-aggressive tone, avoiding the punch of solid-state amps.
blocks.gap: The ideal amp would be an acoustic preamp or DI simulation. US Deluxe provides the cleanest platform available in the catalog.

blocks.purpose: Use a smaller, open-sounding cabinet simulation to maintain intimacy and prevent the sound from becoming overly massive or boomy.
blocks.gap: No specific acoustic IR is available. US 2x12 provides a clean, balanced platform suitable for intimate recordings.

blocks.purpose: No wah or modulation effects are required; the tone must remain natural and dry.
blocks.gap: N/A. Effects should be bypassed.

blocks.purpose: Provide a subtle, natural room ambience to glue the sound together and simulate the recording environment without sounding artificial or cavernous.
blocks.gap: The reverb must be kept very low (low mix) to maintain the 'dry' feel of the original studio recording.

blocks.purpose: No delay is needed; the focus must remain on the immediate, natural sound of the arpeggios.
blocks.gap: N/A. Bypass to maintain dryness.

blocks.purpose: Final output level adjustment to match the intimate and balanced dynamics of the original recording.
blocks.gap: N/A. Standard final stage control.

warnings: The source material is purely acoustic (acoustic guitar). This rig uses an electric guitar input and simulates the tone using clean, vintage amp models and room ambience to achieve a playable approximation of the required intimate folk sound.

improvements.summary: Replace generic IR with an acoustic-focused cabinet simulation for better realism.

proposals.reason: The current US 2x12 is too generic; a dedicated acoustic IR will improve natural string clarity.
